generation.scope: At rank ten a four-support center followed by a second conic forces its unique first-line forward center to be ternary of singular pencil type. Its third curve and next position are planar; a cubic third curve has a backward center at its double point. Independently of rank, a singular ternary center identifies projected coordinates on the next pair. After a twisted cubic its third degree is between two and four (at most three if the projection center lies on the cubic), by the length-one bound for paths returning to their fixed start.

open_mathematics: Use the now forced next centers and projections to restrict the terminal directed components at rank ten, in particular regular ternary pencils and binary centers paired with their reverse centers. For finite reduced rank ten resolve the unequal symmetric triples; extend five-space support arguments to nonreduced graphs.
